prompt:
Edit image 1 directly into a compact BLACKSMITH WORKSHOP prop belonging to the EXACT same game asset set. Image 1 is the sole master for wood colour, metal colour, painted material treatment, geometric style, camera and proportions. Image 2 is ONLY the fabric colour reference (Eni's rust/terracotta apron, cream shirt, ochre sash), not a person to include.

MOST IMPORTANT: preserve image 1's existing wooden workbench and its colours, grain strokes, chunky bevels, warm brown/ochre planes and dark iron bands almost pixel-for-pixel wherever possible. This is a functional conversion of THIS PARTICULAR merchant stall, NOT a reinterpretation from verbal style tags. Do not recolour, desaturate, brighten or redesign the wood. Match both dark brown board faces and amber edge planes from image 1 exactly. Preserve its hand-painted stylized 3D asset appearance and broad purposeful brushwork, NOT grey weathered realistic wood, NOT photorealistic textures, NOT glossy yellow plastic or flat featureless surfaces.

Replace the shop goods with a very small amount of blacksmith equipment: remove ALL sacks, pottery, fruit, parcels, fabric rolls and storage boxes on top. Retain a broad open worktop made from the SAME existing boards. Put just one large hammer and a pair of tongs together toward the back of the bench, plus a single solid metal billet on the lower shelf. NO ANVIL anywhere, no separate object standing in front. Keep the area in front completely clear.

Replace the rightmost quarter of the counter body with one compact integrated forge in large charcoal-grey / warm-grey stone blocks, with a short tapered stone chimney at the far-right rear. The forge is legible and physically functional with a simple dark firebox opening and a few chunky unlit coals, no fire or glow. New stone uses broad sculpted planes and sparse painted edge wear matching the simple dark iron on image 1; avoid pale beige stone and uniform high-contrast white bevel lines. Chimney height similar to the canopy ridge. No busy brickwork or scattered rubble.

Keep the small rear GABLED canopy and its straight ridge / chunky A-frame timber supports from image 1, resizing only as needed to sit over the left workbench with forge beside it. Its fabric changes from olive to the precise rust-red/terracotta of Eni's apron in image 2, with a narrow plain cream edge inspired by her shirt; the fabric still has image 1's simple broad planar folds. Do not copy any emblems or patterns. No arched canopy supports. No front posts. Roof must not hide worktop from the high camera.

Add exactly ONE compact hanging square lantern at the upper-left outer timber support, hung from a stout dark iron hook. Small dark iron frame, four broad amber glass panels, simple cross-bracing, no bloom, no light cast onto timber. It is visibly a hanging fixture, not a large lamp on the worktop. No other lights.

Preserve the full single-asset 3/4 high orthographic composition from image 1. Entire object with all feet visible, clean transparent margin all around, no crop. Genuine transparent alpha background INCLUDING gaps between legs and canopy supports. No floor, scenery, ground slab, shadow catcher, cast ground shadow, vignette, text, watermark, people, flags, signs, heraldry. Neutral even material presentation, no sunset colour grade. Exactly one assembled workshop on the canvas, no grids or alternate views.
